reason: The text demonstrates collaboration between Gideon (the leader) and the Israelite people at multiple points: (1) Gideon sends messengers to summon the tribes of Manasseh, Asher, Zebulun, and Naphtali, and they respond by rising up to join him; (2) The 300 selected men execute Gideon's unified battle strategy, dividing into three groups and following his explicit instructions ('Look at me and do likewise'); (3) The men of Ephraim cooperate with Gideon's forces to intercept and capture the Midianite leaders Oreb and Zeeb. The narrative shows systematic coordination between the leader and multiple groups of people working toward a common goal of defeating the enemy.
